source.verse_hash_method: SHA-256 of the exact original XML verse substring, including written/read notes, not a normalized substitute.
source.public_versification_note: Public and Hebrew numbering align throughout Numbers 3–4. All 100 exact original records are hashed, including annotations at 3:30 and 3:39, with the extraordinary dots on and Aaron retained in the original bytes. Later book numbering differences require separate mapping.

key_decisions.decision: Retains the thirty-to-fifty age range and renders tsava as organized sanctuary service here rather than military duty.
Renders the holy-of-holies phrase as the sacred objects described next, not permission to enter the inner chamber.
Preserves the ark’s unique outer blue layer and sequence; retains uncertain taḥash and notes the pole instruction alongside Exodus 25:15.
Makes covering-before-carrying explicit and keeps the warning of death from touching, distinct from an execution command.
Retains cut-off language with permissive force in context, making the leaders’ protective responsibility audible.
Keeps the positive and negative life/death purpose, priestly action and each man’s individually assigned work and burden.
Identifies the otherwise ambiguous they and retains the death warning; notes the alternative reading while the holy things are being covered.
Keeps the repeated age limits and organized service criterion without confusing this count with chapter 3’s infants-and-up census.
Preserves the same age band and sanctuary service criteria in the source’s repeated formula.
Retains small components and named item assignment; does not quietly shift by-name from equipment to personnel.
Retains the full repeated age and service scope in the report of compliance.
Retains the repeated thirty-to-fifty criterion and sanctuary work, rather than replacing it with an abbreviated reference.
Preserves the final group’s complete age and service criterion with matching English for the repeated Hebrew.
Retains the repeated age band and the summary’s distinction between service work and carrying work.
Unfolds the compressed final clause as a registration summary without silently changing the Hebrew; a note identifies its difficult syntax.
